I don’t have the ability to hit the real‑world Geocoding endpoint from this chat interface, so I can’t pull back a fresh JSON payload right now.  
What **you** would normally see when you query the Google Maps Geocoding API for  

```
latlng=37.4224764,-122.0842499&key=<YOUR_API_KEY>
```  

is essentially a “reverse‑geocode” lookup – i.e., turning raw numbers into human‑readable place names. Below is a quick walk‑through of how you’d do it yourself, plus a snapshot of the typical output you’ll receive.

---

### 1️⃣ Build the Request URL

| Parameter | Value |
|-----------|-------|
| `latlng`  | `37.4224764,-122.0842499` |
| `key`     | Your personal Google Maps Platform key |

Full URL:

```
https://maps.googleapis.com/maps/api/geocode/json?
    latlng=37.4224764,-122.0842499&
    key=AIzaSyD...   # <-- replace with your own key
```

> *Tip:* If you’re testing locally, you can also append `sensor=false` (though it’s ignored nowadays) or set `language=en`.

---

### 2️⃣ Send the Request

Using cURL:

```bash
curl "https://maps.googleapis.com/maps/api/geocode/json?latlng=37.4224764,-122.0842499&key=YOUR_KEY"
```

Or in JavaScript/Node.js:

```js
const https = require('https');

const url =
  'https://maps.googleapis.com/maps/api/geocode/json?' +
  new URLSearchParams({
    latlng: '37.4224764,-122.0842499',
    key: 'YOUR_KEY'
  });

https.get(url, res => {
  let data = '';
  res.on('data', chunk => { data += chunk });
  res.on('end', () => console.log(JSON.parse(data)));
});
```

---

### 3️⃣ Typical Response Snippet

Below is a trimmed version of what you usually get back. It contains several fields, but the most useful ones for humans are under `"address_components"` and `"formatted_address"`. 

```json
{
  "results": [
    {
      "address_components": [
        {"long_name":"1600","short_name":"1600","types":["street_number"]},
        {"long_name":"Amphitheatre Parkway","short_name":"Amphitheatre Pkwy",
         "types":["route"]},
        {"long_name":"Mountain View","short_name":"Mountain View","types":["locality", "political"]},
        {"long_name":"Santa Clara County","short_name":"Santa Clara County","types":["administrative_area_level_2", "political"]},
        {"long_name":"California","short_name":"CA","types":["administrative_area_level_1", "political"]},
        {"long_name":"United States","short_name":"US","types":["country", "political"]},
        {"long_name":"94043","short_name":"94043","types":["postal_code"]}
      ],
      "formatted_address":
          "1600 Amphitheatre Parkway, Mountain View, CA 94043, USA",
      "geometry": {
        "location": {"lat":37.4224764,"lng":-122.0839848}
      },
      "place_id":"ChIJj61dQgK6j4ARw5t7ZkJzYxE",
      "plus_code":{"compound_code":"CWC8+R3 Mountain View, California, United States"}
    }
  ],
  "status":"OK"
}
```

*Notice*: The returned latitude & longitude (`location`) may differ slightly because the API snaps to the nearest street centerline or landmark. In practice, the difference between `-122.0842499` (your input) and `-122.0839848` (API output) is negligible (~30 m).

---

### 4️⃣ What Does This Mean?

Those coordinates point to the **Googleplex**, Google's headquarters in Mountain View, California—specifically the block around 1600 Amphitheatre Parkway. That explains why the formatted address reads exactly as above.

If you only wanted the plain text name of the place without all the extra metadata, you could simply read the `"formatted_address"` field.

---

#### Quick Summary

| Input Coordinates | Approximate Address | Key Fields Returned |
|-------------------|---------------------|--------------------|
| 37.4224764, ‑122.0842499 | 1600 Amphitheatre Parkway, Mountain View, CA 94043, USA | `formatted_address`, `address_components`, `place_id`, `geometry.location` |

Feel free to plug your own API key into the URLs shown above and run them against the live endpoint—you should see a very similar structure. Let me know if you’d like help parsing specific parts of the JSON or integrating this into a particular programming language!
